item.title: Chand tells Education Ministry: Stop excuses, pay teachers
item.description: Opposition MP Hem Chand has called on the Ministry of Education to take responsibility for delays in paying teachers, saying administrative problems should not result in educators going without salaries they have already earned. Chand said teachers and their families should not have to bear the consequences of delays within the Ministry.
item.content:encoded:
Opposition MP Hem Chand has called on the Ministry of Education to take responsibility for delays in paying teachers, saying administrative problems should not result in educators going without salaries they have already earned.

Chand said teachers and their families should not have to bear the consequences of delays within the Ministry.

“How long must our teachers continue to wait for the salaries they have rightfully earned?” Chand asked.

“The Ministry of Education must stop hiding behind excuses and take responsibility for the unacceptable delays in paying teachers.”

His comments follow confirmation from the Ministry that salary arrears owed to 318 staff members would be paid under Pay 17 and Pay 18.

Education Minister Aseri Radrodro had said common issues identified in processing arrears included the absence of Fiji Teachers Registration Authority registration certificates, missing bank details and delays in confirmation of officers commencing duties from Heads of Schools or District Education Officers.

Chand rejected those issues as sufficient justification for prolonged salary delays.

“Excuses such as missing FTRA registration certificates or bank details cannot justify teachers being left without their salaries for months,” he said.

“If there are administrative problems, the Ministry must fix them urgently rather than allowing teachers and their families to bear the consequences of bureaucratic failures.”

Chand said teachers were simply seeking payment for work they had already performed.

“Teachers are not asking for a favour. They are asking for what they have already earned,” he said.

He also questioned the Coalition Government’s commitment to supporting educators when some teachers were experiencing salary delays.

“The Coalition Government has repeatedly spoken about improving education and supporting our teachers. But what message are we sending when hardworking teachers cannot even receive their salaries on time?”

“Teachers’ welfare must be a priority — not an afterthought.”

Chand called on the Education Minister to ensure all outstanding salaries were settled without further delay.

“I call on the Minister for Education to stop the excuses, take responsibility and ensure that all outstanding teacher salaries are paid immediately,” he said.

He also called on Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka to personally intervene and seek an urgent resolution.

“A government that values education must value the people who deliver it,” Chand said.

“Our teachers deserve dignity. Our teachers deserve respect. Our teachers deserve to be paid on time.”

Chand concluded his statement with a direct demand: “Enough of the excuses. Enough of the delays. Pay our teachers — now!”

item.title: Scammers impersonate LTA in text messages, alert issued
item.description: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is warning members of the public about a scam text message being circulated claiming to be a notification of a Traffic Infringement Notice (TIN). LTA Chief Executive Officer Irimaia Rokosawa said the message was not legitimate and urged members of the public not to click on, respond to or share any links contained in the suspicious SMS.
item.content:encoded:
The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is warning members of the public about a scam text message being circulated claiming to be a notification of a Traffic Infringement Notice (TIN).

LTA Chief Executive Officer Irimaia Rokosawa said the message was not legitimate and urged members of the public not to click on, respond to or share any links contained in the suspicious SMS.

“The Authority does not send TINs via unofficial links or through suspicious senders, and any such communication should be treated as a scam,” he said.

The Authority is urging members of the public to exercise caution when receiving unsolicited messages from unknown or suspicious senders, particularly those demanding immediate payment or payment within a specified timeframe.

LTA said members of the public should verify any information relating to traffic infringements directly with the Authority through its official channels.

“Members of the public are urged to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgment when confronted with suspicious communications or requests for suspicious payments through URL links.”

LTA advised anyone who receives a suspicious text message claiming to be from the Authority to report it immediately to the relevant authorities.

“Do not engage or make payment without first verifying with the Authority.”

The Authority said protecting the safety and security of its customers remained a priority.

“Your vigilance helps prevent fraud. Always rely on verified and official LTA channels for traffic and infringement matters.”

item.title: Attempted murder accused arrested in Nasinu
item.description: Saimoni Rokotunidau, who is charged with the attempted murder of Police Constable Senoveva Tikoduadua and was wanted on a bench warrant, has been arrested. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe confirmed that Rokotunidau was arrested this morning at a residence along Nasinu Road.
item.content:encoded:
Saimoni Rokotunidau, who is charged with the attempted murder of Police Constable Senoveva Tikoduadua and was wanted on a bench warrant, has been arrested.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe confirmed that Rokotunidau was arrested this morning at a residence along Nasinu Road.

“Bench warrantee Saimoni Rokotunidau was arrested this morning by officers from the Serious Organised Crime, K9 and Valelevu CID at a residence in Nasinu Road,” ACP Vusonilawe said.

Rokotunidau had earlier failed to appear in court despite being required to do so under his bail conditions.

State lawyer Hezekiah Nofaga had informed High Court judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere that Rokotunidau was on the run and had also sold the property where he had been residing.

The State subsequently applied for Rokotunidau’s two sureties to be summoned before the court to explain why he had failed to attend court despite the conditions attached to his bail.

Justice Tuiqereqere granted the application and ordered the two sureties to appear in court on August 25 to explain Rokotunidau’s non-attendance.

Rokotunidau is facing an attempted murder charge in relation to an incident involving Police Constable Senoveva Tikoduadua at a checkpoint in Laqere, Nasinu, in April.

Constable Tikoduadua, the daughter of Defence and Veterans Affairs Minister Pio Tikoduadua, was struck by a vehicle while manning the checkpoint.

The vehicle was allegedly being pursued by police at the time of the incident.

Rokotunidau’s arrest follows efforts by police to locate him after the bench warrant was issued.

item.title: 318 Education ministry staff finally getting paid
item.description: The Ministry of Education has confirmed that salary arrears owed to 318 staff members will be paid under Pay 17 and Pay 18, following delays caused by internal and compliance issues. Education Minister Aseri Radrodro said the Ministry had expedited the processing of the outstanding payments.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Education has confirmed that salary arrears owed to 318 staff members will be paid under Pay 17 and Pay 18, following delays caused by internal and compliance issues.

Education Minister Aseri Radrodro said the Ministry had expedited the processing of the outstanding payments.

Radrodro said some of the delays were linked to incomplete documentation required to process appointments and salaries.

“The common issues identified during the processing of payment of arrears are the absence of FTRA registration certificates, lack of bank details, and the absence of timely submission of confirmation of officers’ commencement of duty from their respective Heads of Schools and/or District Education Officers,” he said.

He urged affected teachers to provide the necessary documentation, including confirmation of their appointment and commencement date from their Head of School or respective District Education Officer.

Radrodro said the Ministry had also undertaken due diligence to ensure all appointments were formally processed and that there was no incomplete documentation.

“I wish to advise all teachers that they need to understand that all appointments are formally processed and signed by PS Education prior to reporting to schools. This should allow for smooth processing of their appointments in our HR Department and for processing of their pays,” he said.

The Minister acknowledged the continued dedication of teachers working in schools across Fiji and thanked them for their commitment to providing quality education to students.

He also acknowledged the approval by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka for the payment of the salary arrears.

Radrodro said the Ministry would continue to streamline its expenditure controls while ensuring staff welfare remained a priority.

“I wish to assure all our MOE Staff that their welfare remains a priority for this Ministry. The arrears of salary payment is not only a financial recognition, but also a reaffirmation of the Coalition Government’s appreciation for the critical roles in the lives of educating our children,” he said.

The Minister also thanked education stakeholders and teacher unions for their continued support, collaboration and understanding.

item.title: MPs not above parking rules: Minister Bainivalu
item.description: Members of Parliament are not above parking rules or other lawful requirements within the parliamentary precincts, says Minister for Forests and Fisheries Alitia Bainivalu. Bainivalu made the comments on social media in response to Opposition MP Jone Usamate, who accused police of overreach after receiving a parking ticket while attending to parliamentary duties.
item.content:encoded:
Members of Parliament are not above parking rules or other lawful requirements within the parliamentary precincts, says Minister for Forests and Fisheries Alitia Bainivalu.

Bainivalu made the comments on social media in response to Opposition MP Jone Usamate, who accused police of overreach after receiving a parking ticket while attending to parliamentary duties.

“Parliamentary privilege does not mean that Members of Parliament are above parking rules or other lawful requirements within the Parliamentary precincts,” Bainivalu said.

She said that after seeing a photograph circulating on social media showing where Usamate’s vehicle had been parked, the incident appeared to be a case of an officer carrying out their duties rather than police interference.

“Hon. Jone Usamate, having now seen the photo circulating on social media showing where the vehicle was parked, this appears less like a case of ‘police overreach’ and more like a police officer simply doing their job,” she said.

Usamate had earlier criticised police after receiving the ticket, saying he had been parked within the parliamentary precincts while carrying out the work he was elected to do.

Bainivalu rejected that argument and instead questioned whether Usamate’s vehicle had the required Parliamentary Vehicle Pass clearly displayed.

“The simple question remains: Was the Parliamentary Vehicle Pass clearly displayed on the dashboard at the time the vehicle was fined?” she asked.

“If the required pass was not displayed, how was the police officer expected to know that the vehicle belonged to a Member of Parliament and was authorised to park there?”

Bainivalu said police officers had a responsibility to enforce the law and maintain order and should be permitted to perform those duties without individual enforcement actions automatically becoming political disputes.

“Our police officers have a responsibility to enforce the law and maintain order,” she said.

“They should be allowed to do their work without every enforcement action being turned into a political argument about the separation of powers.”

item.title: FEO admits internal procedures not followed over mock election release
item.description: The Fijian Elections Office has acknowledged that required internal procedures were not followed when a mock press release containing a fictitious 2026 General Election date was uploaded to its website. In a statement, the FEO said the release was created as part of a Writ to Return of Writ Dress Rehearsal being conducted in preparation for the upcoming General Election.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Elections Office has acknowledged that required internal procedures were not followed when a mock press release containing a fictitious 2026 General Election date was uploaded to its website.

In a statement, the FEO said the release was created as part of a Writ to Return of Writ Dress Rehearsal being conducted in preparation for the upcoming General Election.

“The FEO acknowledges that the required internal procedure for uploading test content was not followed,” the statement said.

“The matter has since been addressed internally, and measures are being taken to ensure that test materials used during the remainder of the Dress Rehearsal are appropriately contained.”

The clarification follows the circulation of the mock release by media organisations and subsequently on social media.

The FEO said its current dress rehearsal requires staff to test, review, finalise and lock in processes that will be followed from the issuance of the Writ of Election through to the Return of the Writ.

As part of that exercise, staff tested procedures for preparing and publishing press releases.

A mock release relating to the issuance of the Writ was created on the FEO website using fictitious information for the simulation.

The release included a purported election date, which the FEO has now stressed was not genuine.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the information contained in the mock press release, including the date stated for the General Election, was entirely fictitious and created solely for the purposes of the Dress Rehearsal,” the FEO said.

“No Writ for the 2026 General Election has been issued.”

The FEO said one of the key purposes of conducting a dress rehearsal was to expose weaknesses in its systems and processes before the actual election period.

“The main purpose of conducting a Dress Rehearsal is to identify gaps and subsequently the necessary safeguards required to ensure they do not happen during the actual Election Period,” it said.

The Elections Office has apologised for the confusion caused by the publication and subsequent circulation of the mock release.

“The FEO apologises for any confusion caused and assures all electoral stakeholders and more importantly members of the public that the matter has been addressed.”

The FEO said safeguards were now being put in place to ensure test material produced during the remainder of the dress rehearsal is appropriately contained and does not enter the public domain.

item.title: Calls for clear rules on AI election forecasts
item.description: Transparency Fiji and Integrity Fiji are calling on the Electoral Commission to urgently clarify how AI-generated election forecasts will be regulated ahead of Fiji’s next General Election, warning that such predictions could potentially influence voter choices and the wider electoral environment. The call follows concerns raised by the Fijian Elections Office that AI-generated predictions could i
item.content:encoded:
Transparency Fiji and Integrity Fiji are calling on the Electoral Commission to urgently clarify how AI-generated election forecasts will be regulated ahead of Fiji’s next General Election, warning that such predictions could potentially influence voter choices and the wider electoral environment.

The call follows concerns raised by the Fijian Elections Office that AI-generated predictions could influence undecided voters, affect voter turnout and create a misleading impression of certainty about election outcomes.

“Our elections belong to the people. Technology can inform a voter, but it must never take away the voter’s freedom to choose,” said the two organisations.

The organisations said the principle of protecting a voter’s independent choice was already reflected in Fiji’s Electoral Act 2014.

It pointed to provisions governing assistance for voters with disabilities, saying while another person may assist a voter, that person is not permitted to influence how the voter votes.

They said a similar principle should now be considered when dealing with artificial intelligence and other forms of political technology.

“If information or predictions are deliberately designed, presented or amplified in a manner that improperly influences voters, this raises serious questions about the integrity of the electoral process.”

They are calling on the Electoral Commission to clarify how AI-generated election forecasts and predictive models will be treated under Sections 110 and 110A of the Electoral Act 2014.

TIF said that clarification should come well before the final stages of the election period.

“The Electoral Commission should clarify the rules now, before AI-generated forecasts become capable of influencing the electoral environment, rather than waiting until the final seven days when it may be too late,” it said.

According to TIF, Section 110A provides for guidelines relating to election-related opinion polls, surveys and research, while Section 110 restricts publication of election-related opinion poll results during the final seven days of the election period.

TIF said advances in artificial intelligence meant systems could now generate sophisticated election forecasts using information including historical election results, political trends, social-media sentiment, perceptions of leadership credibility, party resources and voter behaviour.

This made it increasingly important for the public to understand exactly what type of information was being presented to them.

TIF said voters should be able to distinguish between “a verified fact, an opinion poll, statistical modelling or a prediction.”

The organisation stressed that it was not seeking to prohibit the use of artificial intelligence in election-related discussion.

“TIF is not calling for a ban on AI. We are calling for transparency, accountability and clear rules,” it said.

It said early clarification from the Electoral Commission would provide greater certainty over the use and publication of AI-generated forecasts while helping safeguard voters’ ability to make their electoral choices independently.

item.title: Usamate accuses Police of overreach after parliament parking fine
item.description: Opposition MP Jone Usamate has accused police of overreach after receiving a parking ticket for his vehicle while carrying out parliamentary duties within the parliamentary precincts. In a social media post, Usamate questioned the authority of police to issue the fine within Parliament and called on the Minister responsible for policing and the Commissioner of Police to address the matter.
item.content:encoded:
Opposition MP Jone Usamate has accused police of overreach after receiving a parking ticket for his vehicle while carrying out parliamentary duties within the parliamentary precincts.

In a social media post, Usamate questioned the authority of police to issue the fine within Parliament and called on the Minister responsible for policing and the Commissioner of Police to address the matter.

“Fined by the police for parking in the parliamentary precincts while doing my job,” Usamate said.

“Parliament is a separate legislative arm of the state, and the police have no right to interfere with the separation of powers.”

Usamate said he received the parking ticket after coming out of Parliament, where he had been carrying out work relating to justice and human rights.

“I get a parking ticket given by the police for parking in parliamentary precincts,” he said.

“So it seems the police is telling me, as a member of Parliament, not to park in parliamentary precincts to do the work that I’m elected to do.”

Usamate called for intervention from the Minister and Commissioner of Police and questioned the conduct of the officers involved.

“I request the Minister and the Commissioner of Police to do something about this,” he said.

“These police officers need to be pinned about how they carry out their jobs.”

The Opposition MP argued that Parliament’s position as the legislative arm of the State needed to be respected.

“Parliament on its own is a legislative arm of the State. Nobody, including the police, they don’t have any right to do this in parliamentary precincts,” Usamate said.

He described the incident as “very poor” and raised concerns about the separation of powers.

Usamate has called on the authorities to address what he considers police interference within the parliamentary precincts.
